answer: A reef grows strong only when polyps build on a shared basalt skeleton, and an agent economy can borrow that shape: each identity is bonded to a trellis of cross-guarantees where established peers stake their own standing to vouch for a newcomer. Convicting one sybil slashes every guarantor in its chain, so collateral cannot be pooled across a farm. The cost to an attacker grows with the square of identity count, because each new clone must recruit a fresh, unlinked bond tree, and honest agents refuse to build beside rubble.
